headline: High: Dexter’s autonomous, broad-network execution can leak or act on Dagster-produced data, while Dagster provides no runtime isolation or output verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dagster has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, browser, or MCP surfaces, so direct injection into it is unlikely. Dexter can autonomously execute and consume files in .dexter/scratchpad/, so only a manual or file-based bridge exists. The pairwise pathway is therefore limited and not default-dangerous.
conditions: IF an operator copies Dexter output into Dagster-managed content or shared files
IF Dagster is extended to ingest scratchpad files as trusted instructions
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Do not copy Dexter outputs into Dagster inputs without review
Rename scratchpad files to non-executable, non-instructional formats
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between file producers and consumers

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dagster touches no data classes and has no network egress, but Dexter handles financial and market data, uses multiple external APIs, and has broad network egress. If Dagster and Dexter share a workspace or hand off files, Dexter can transmit that content to third parties. The interaction is plausible but not proven from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF Dagster writes sensitive pipeline artifacts into a directory Dexter reads
IF Dexter is configured to send shared files or prompts to OpenAI, Exa, Tavily, or Financial Datasets APIs
mitigations: Separate workspaces and mount points
Restrict Dexter API keys to non-sensitive test data
Disable sharing of Dagster artifacts into .dexter/scratchpad/
Review outbound API destinations before runs
requires-engineering: add per-directory access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dagster cannot write files, modify git state, or use MCP, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. Dexter supports multiple instances and has a scratchpad directory plus API calls, but the pair lacks overlapping write authority in the profiles. Any conflict would require extra orchestration not shown here.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory
IF Dexter and Dagster are both wrapped with additional mutable resource permissions
mitigations: Keep Dagster read-only in shared environments
Avoid giving Dexter write access to Dagster-managed paths
Serialize any shared-resource operations
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dagster is a data orchestrator, so its outputs can become downstream inputs, while Dexter runs autonomously and can act on API results. If Dexter consumes Dagster-produced artifacts without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect research outputs or actions. The profiles do not show a built-in verification gate, so the pathway exists in default-style workflows.
conditions: IF Dexter treats Dagster-produced artifacts as authoritative inputs
IF no human or automated verification step checks Dagster outputs before Dexter uses them
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents
Require schema checks on Dagster outputs
Limit Dexter to read-only analysis of Dagster artifacts
Add human review for high-impact actions
requires-engineering: implement signed handoff artifacts

E_compliance.rationale: Dexter explicitly handles financial and market data and uses third-party APIs, which can create residency, retention, or logging mismatches. Dagster’s profile shows no data classes touched and no network egress, so it is not the compliance driver here. The risk is mainly Dexter-side, but the pair can still violate policy if Dagster feeds regulated data into Dexter.
conditions: IF Dagster supplies regulated or region-restricted data to Dexter
IF Dexter API logging or retention exceeds the operator’s policy for financial data
mitigations: Do not route regulated data into Dexter
Review API retention settings for each Dexter provider
Use synthetic or anonymized datasets
Document data residency for each external API
requires-engineering: enforce policy-based routing and retention controls
